# `silk/http/server_native`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

Accepts native socket connections and serves each one with `silk.http.server`.

## When to use
Make a listener with `silk.net.socket_native`, then call [`serveNext`](#serveNext) in a loop. Each call accepts
one connection and serves it with your `ConnectionHandler` until the handler returns.

## Details
[`serveNext`](#serveNext) serves one connection at a time, on the calling task. This module has no queue,
router, supervisor, or background task. To serve connections at the same time, start tasks
yourself.

## Errors
- `NativeSocketError` if the accept fails or the deadline passes.
- `ServerError`, `BufferError`, and `OutOfMemoryError` from `silk.http.server`.
- The error of the handler.

## Gotchas
The module exists on Windows x86_64 with the system runtime, Darwin aarch64, and Linux with
GNU libc on x86_64 or aarch64. On other targets, an import from it fails to compile.

Import as `HttpServerNative` with `import silk.http.server_native { HttpServerNative }`.

Public declarations: 2.

## `serveNext`

```silk
pub effect<'env> fn serveNext<
    'listener,
    A,
    E,
    ?HandlerRequirements,
    H: ConnectionHandler<NativeConnection, A, E ? HandlerRequirements> + 'env,
    'env,
  >(
    listener: &'listener mut Listener,
    limits: Limits,
    acceptDeadline: Option<Instant>,
    handler: H,
  ) -> A
  ! E | NativeSocketError | ServerError | BufferError | OutOfMemoryError
  ? HandlerRequirements | &mut Allocator | &mut MonotonicClock
  where HandlerRequirements in Without<HandlerRequirements, ByteDuplex>
```

Accepts one connection from `listener`, and serves it with `handler`.

### Details
The accept waits until `acceptDeadline`, or with no limit if it is `None`. Then it calls
`withConnection` of `silk.http.server` with `limits`. The socket is closed when the handler
returns or fails. Call it in a loop. It serves one connection at a time, on the calling task,
with no queue, router, supervisor, or background task. To serve connections at the same time,
start tasks yourself.

### Errors
- `NativeSocketError` if the accept fails or the deadline passes.
- `ServerError`, `BufferError`, and `OutOfMemoryError` from `silk.http.server`.
- The error of the handler.

### Gotchas

It exists on Windows x86_64 with the system runtime, Darwin aarch64, and Linux with
GNU libc on x86_64 or aarch64.
